Subject: Launch Ramp: VPC & on-prem rollout prep — account and validation sweep

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We are ready to begin firm planning for our private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge). Before we lock dates, the Security and Cloud teams asked for a short, prescriptive list of account-level prerequisites and the environment validation items your team will need to sign off on.

Can you send a checklist we can share with Procurement and our infra leads? Also include the network ranges, required service accounts/roles, KMS key expectations, and any evidence you typically collect for SOC-type reviews. If you have a run template for a first smoke validation, that would be great.

Our tentative window is the week of Dec 7th — we want to confirm a tentative kickoff and get the procurement contacts looped in.

Thanks,
Lillian Shaw
VP, Cloud Platforms
Novus Health

Subject: Re: Launch Ramp: VPC & on-prem rollout prep — account and validation sweep

Hi Lillian —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've attached our "Launch Ramp" checklist (spreadsheet) and a lightweight validation-run template. High level notes below so your teams can triage quickly: 

Account & networking essentials (quick reference):
- Dedicated project/account: create a dedicated cloud project or account to host Redwood Private control plane connectors and any outbound egress gateways.
- IP ranges: provide a /22 for service egress and a separate /24 for management plane peering (we can accept CIDR overlap constraints but prefer non-overlapping).
- Firewall: outbound TLS (443) to our control plane IPs + ephemeral ports for health checks; inbound only for specific management channels if you opt for direct peering.
- NAT & Egress: ensure SNAT for outbound worker traffic; list of egress FQDNs in the attached sheet.
- Service accounts & roles: one service principal for deployment automation (roles: compute.admin, network.admin, storage.admin, kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter), plus a read-only audit account.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed key preferred; we require key wrap/unlock for disk images and secrets that persist in the environment.
- Audit logs: enable VPC flow logs and admin activity logs retained for minimum 90 days (we'll provide retention guidance if you need 365-day evidence).

Validation & acceptance gates (summary):
1) Account provisioning and IAM alignment (validate roles & service accounts).
2) Network reachability and route table sanity (ping/traceroute matrix in template).
3) KMS access and sample encrypt/decrypt operation.
4) Bootstrap deployment into a sandbox tenant and pass smoke tests (model load, inference latency baseline, KV cache warm).
5) Audit evidence collection: logs, IAM snapshots, and s3/bucket access proofs.

I've attached: launch-ramp-checklist.xlsx (tabbed: prerequisites, network-ips, evidence), validation-run-template.yaml, and a quick network diagram (PNG).

Proposed next steps:
- Procurement contact: loop them (cc'd) and confirm any purchase order or channel steps.
- Tech checkpoint: Ben will pick up the technical intake and propose a scoped validation window.
- Kickoff slot: Dec 7-9 are acceptable from our side; we'll lock a 90-minute kickoff with infra, security, and procurement.

If helpful I can prepare a one-page "evidence packet" format for SOC review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: launch-ramp-checklist.xlsx; validation-run-template.yaml; network-diagram.png

Thanks Marissa / Lillian — quick technical clarifications from my side before we hand this to the intake sprint: 

- Can Novus confirm whether the management plane peering will be direct VPC peering or via a transit/gateway? Transit is fine but we need to know if asymmetric routing will exist.
- Please include the expected peak concurrent QPS and 95th percentile request size (tokens) for the first two weeks of validation — we use that to select initial node sizing and batching profiles.
- VLAN tagging: if on-prem will be colocated, a list of VLAN IDs or a VLAN provisioning ticket helps us pre-populate the service mapping.
- DNS: we prefer a customer-created CNAME for control-plane callbacks; if you cannot create DNS records, we can provide signed-cert fallback.

I've updated the validation-run-template.yaml with fields for qps/token-size and added a small checklist for KV cache warming (this is commonly missed). Quoted below is Marissa's checklist for quick reference.

> - Service accounts & roles: one service principal for deployment automation (roles: compute.admin, network.admin, storage.admin, kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter), plus a read-only audit account.

Ben Carter

Thanks — this is excellent and actionable. We're confirming an internal slot on Nov 30th for the procurement review and aiming to lock technical kickoff in the Dec 7th window. Procurement folks (cc'd) will start the PO and contract checklist; they may ask about the SLA and data residency (Novus needs all PHI processed in the us-east-1 footprint).

Answers to Ben's clarifications:
- Management plane: we prefer transit-gateway for enterprise routing; there will be asymmetric egress via our outbound NAT.
- Initial traffic profile: 200 QPS peak, 95th percentile request ~1.8k tokens. We'll send detailed traffic curves by EOD Nov 12.
- VLANs: on-prem team will publish VLAN IDs and edge switch ports next week.
- DNS: we can add a CNAME for callbacks to the provided control-plane name.

Procurement: can you send a short one-page list of items you'd like included in the PO (licenses, reserved capacity, on-prem support days, optional add-ons)? That will speed our internal approval.

Look forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Lillian
VP, Cloud Platforms
Novus Health
